findings.title: Rescored on M30 prices, 24 Nov
findings.body: 57 alerts scored from their own levels. T1: 1 target, 23 stops, 12 open (avg -0.85R). T2: 1 target, 2 stops, 2 open. T3: 3 targets, 4 stops, 9 open (avg +0.57R). T1 buys: 0 wins of 17. Giveback 30% after +1R keeps T3 at 12 wins of 14 but T1 stays weak. Ten earlier outcomes changed, 4 of them wins that were really stops. Small samples.

findings.title: CVD divergence plus MA cross, M30 test (24 Nov)
findings.body: Tested on the 11 M30 CSVs (5 to 24 Nov): a bullish or bearish CVD divergence (price moves against the CVD over 8 bars) followed by an MA cross in the reversal direction, stop at the 10-bar swing, target 2R. Result: 85 trades, 31 wins, average -0.02R. The same MA cross with no divergence: 186 trades, 69 wins, average +0.01R. EURUSD: 6 trades, 2 wins, -0.30R. USDCAD: 5 trades, 1 win, -0.40R. Divergence adds nothing in this sample. PC crosses are not in the CSV, so they were not tested. Small sample, my own divergence definition.

findings.title: T2 is the only tier with a clean record so far
findings.body: T2: 4 targets, 0 stops, 2 still open. T1: 3 targets, 18 stops. T3: 0 targets, 5 stops. T3 also has 3 open and 2 unclear.

findings.title: T2 is 6 alerts, and 3 of its wins are one USDJPY rally
findings.body: The three USDJPY buys on 9 Nov are one move counted three times. Without them T2 is one win (AUDJPY sell, 13 Nov) and two open sells. Do not call T2 the best signal until it has 20 or more alerts across different days and symbols.

findings.title: T1 buys all lost in one falling week
findings.body: All 15 decided T1 buys were stopped, and all but one were 16 to 19 Nov, when USD and JPY were strong. T1 is meant to fire against the MAs, so in a strong trend it fires into the trend. This says T1 buys lost in this week, not that T1 never works.

findings.title: T1 and T2 and T3 are not independent
findings.body: A T2 or T3 alert follows an EDGE EXH on the same symbol. They are often the same setup seen at different times, so the tiers should be compared per setup, not as separate trades.

findings.title: Scoring is not the same for every row
findings.body: T1 log rows count as stopped if price touched the stop before the opposite alert, with no time cap. T2, T3 and the 3 screenshot T1 sells were read from price on the chart. Some stops and targets in the screenshots were hard to read.

findings.title: Does a T2 after a T1 beat the T1 alone?
findings.body: For each setup, compare the T1 entry with the T2 or T3 entry that followed on the same symbol. If the later entry wins more often, the cross is worth waiting for. Needs more pairs.

findings.title: T1 in the direction of the 4H trend versus against it
findings.body: Add the 4H trend state at each alert and compare. This is the check that would explain the T1 buys.

findings.title: Trend Gate CAUTION
findings.body: 6 of the 20 log T1 alerts carry CAUTION (5 stopped, 1 open). Too few, and non-CAUTION alerts also lost. Keep recording it.

Three alerts is too few to say anything about the rule.

findings.title: CVD quick-sell call (25 Nov, one day)
findings.body: Between the 10:12 and 14:10 charts the dollar rose. EURUSD fell 23 pips, GBPUSD 29, AUDUSD 42, XAUUSD 355 pips (0.1 each) and XAGUSD 101 pips; USDJPY rose 12, USDCAD 15 and USDCHF 11. The 10:15 scan skipped these (4H conflict, or 4H and M30 disagreeing). The trader's view is that a quick sell read from the CVD profile would have paid, and it would have. This is one move on one day, and the USD pairs are one correlation group, so it was one trade under the risk rules. To test it: log each CVD-profile call with time, price and what the profile showed, then score it on the M30 CSV.

method: Each alert is scored from its own entry, target and stop on M30 prices (Premium CSV export, 5 to 24 Nov). First touch wins. On a bar that touches both, the stop counts first. Win = target distance in R, loss = -1R. Open alerts show a Now R and are left out of the win rate and average R. Alerts with missing or reversed levels, or a stop under a quarter of a 4H range, are excluded. Giveback column: after +1R, close when profit falls 30% below the peak profit. A 15-trading-day time limit is planned but no alert has reached it yet. Pips = R times the stop distance (pip = 0.0001, JPY pairs 0.01, gold 0.1, silver 0.01, BTC 1 dollar); open alerts show pips now.
